t: The rates of pay of persons employed by the county committees established pursuant to section 8(b) of the Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act (16 U.S.C. 590h(b)) shall be increased by amounts equal, as nearly as may lie practicable, to the increases provided by section 202(a) of this title for corresponding rates of basic pay.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the reference to "county committees" (farmer-elected local bodies) signals outside participation. But this section only adjusts the pay rates of persons employed by those committees. It does not establish the committees, require consultation, a hearing, a comment period or rulemaking, or grant any right to sue, so no outside party is brought into a federal decision.
fable.s: The rates of pay of persons employed by the county committees established pursuant to section 8(b) of the Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act (16 U.S.C. 590h(b)) shall be increased

qwen_block.w: This section solely addresses the adjustment of pay rates for employees of county committees. It does not establish a process for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. The mention of 'county committees' refers to the employers of the workers whose pay is being adjusted, not to a mechanism for public participation in federal policy.
qwen_block.s: The rates of pay of persons employed by the county committees established pursuant to section 8(b) of the Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act (16 U.S.C. 590h(b)) shall be increased by amounts equal, as nearly as may lie practicable, to the increases provided by section 202(a) of this title for corresponding rates of basic pay.

opus.w: This section only adjusts the pay of people employed by county committees to match federal basic pay increases. It does not have the government consult, coordinate with, or hear from outside parties before making a decision. The committees are mentioned only as employers; the section describes no role for them in shaping a federal decision, so naming them is not participation.
opus.s: The rates of pay of persons employed by the county committees established pursuant to section 8(b) of the Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act (16 U.S.C. 590h(b)) shall be increased by amounts equal, as nearly as may lie practicable, to the increases provided by section 202(a) of this title for corresponding rates of basic pay.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** County committees under section 8(b) of the Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act are made up of locally elected farmers, so their mention might look like outside participation. That reading fails because this section only sets pay increases for people employed by those committees. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or right to sue over any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates a pay increase for employees of county committees based on a statutory formula. It does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from these county committees or any other outside parties before making the decision to increase pay. The county committees are passive recipients of the policy change, not active participants in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: The rates of pay of persons employed by the county committees established pursuant to section 8(b) of the Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act (16 U.S.C. 590h(b)) shall be increased by amounts equal, as nearly as may lie practicable, to the increases provided by section 202(a) of this title for corresponding rates of basic pay.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "county committees" are local government entities, and thus their involvement constitutes participation by outside parties. However, the text does not describe a process where these committees consult with the federal government or participate in a federal decision-making process. Instead, it merely sets the pay rates for employees of these committees. The committees themselves are not engaging in consultation, coordination, or advisory roles with the federal government in this section; they are simply the employers of the persons whose pay is being adjusted. The definition of participation requires the federal government to consult or coordinate with people outside the government *before making a decision*. Here, the federal government is making a decision (setting pay rates) unilaterally, based on a formula, without any input from the county committees.
